fatal_errors: The proposed NbMoTaWVTi composition does not reconstruct the target equimolar CoCrFeNiTi system.

The cited NbMoTaWVTi study reports two BCC solid solutions only in milled powder; after SPS, the bulk material also contains an FCC TiO precipitate phase, so it does not support the claimed dual-BCC-only bulk constitution.
The cited mechanical properties were attributed partly to TiO precipitation strengthening, preventing attribution to nanocrystalline grain-boundary and solid-solution strengthening alone.
No cited evidence establishes a sub-50 nm grain size after SPS, the proposed 1100-1200 degrees C process window, or the stated thermal-stability limits.

The falsification experiment does not distinguish grain-boundary strengthening from simple solid-solution strengthening because temperature changes grain size, phase constitution, precipitation, porosity, and oxygen uptake simultaneously.
explanation: The hypothesis is aligned with the broad processing concept: mechanical alloying followed by rapid SPS is a credible route to refined refractory multi-principal-element alloys, and the cited study directly supports high compressive strength in NbMoTaWVTi. However, it is an alternative alloy rather than a reconstruction of the CoCrFeNiTi target, and its milling duration, SPS temperature, and phase constitution differ substantially. Most importantly, the supporting paper reports TiO precipitation after SPS and attributes part of the strength to that phase, contradicting the proposed dual-solid-solution-only mechanism. The predicted strength values closely reproduce the cited NbMoTaWVTi results, but hardness and retained sub-50 nm bulk grains are unsupported. A discriminating test should produce specimens of identical composition, density, phase fractions, and contamination level but different grain sizes, then test whether yield stress follows a Hall-Petch-type dependence; the proposed broad SPS-temperature sweep cannot isolate that mechanism.
